title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: 10% off promotion on Father's Day
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted promotion lift x1.27 from 7 instances; but 2025 Father's Day promo had only x0.98 lift, suggesting event dampening. Adjusted to x1.15.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 56.3. Father's Day shows no historical lift (x1.0 noise-adjusted), so no adjustment. The 10% promotion has a noise-adjusted lift of x1.27 from 7 past instances, but the 2025 Father's Day week had a 10% promo and only x0.98 lift—suggesting the holiday dampens promotion impact. The 2026-04-27 promo (same price, no holiday) saw x1.89, but that week had no event. The classical model’s x1.27 is too high given the dampening context. Shrinking to x1.15 for the combined effect. The prior week’s promotion (2026-03-23) showed x1.6, but no holiday. The 2025 Father's Day week had a promo and only x0.98, indicating overlap. Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited clean observations. No other drivers. Spreads unchanged.

PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-21 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Father's Day (Sun); Promotion: 10% off
  shelf price: 5.76 (-10.1% vs regular price 6.41)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 56.3 | 5%-95%: 30.9 - 80.0 | 10%-90%: 40.9 - 76.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-31% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
